clue.text: British class established outside the Spanish capital

indicators.note: the British class is set up around the Spanish article, its two parts flanking it

parts.note: a grade is a class or rank
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A British social class has settled around the capital of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'established outside' puts B and GRADE on either side of EL. 'the Spanish capital' looks like Madrid, but 'the Spanish' gives EL and 'capital' alone is the definition: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the seat of government of Serbia, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Tramp? That's my neighour in a game

definitions.text: That's my neighour in a game

explanation.surface: A down-and-out is introduced as the neighbour in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: Beggar-my-neighbour is a children's card game, so the word that goes before 'my neighbour' in its name is the second definition. 'neighour' is printed without its second b.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a vagrant who asks for money, and the card game Beggar-my-neighbour has this word at the front of its name.

clue.text: Come down to a university in old-fashioned carriage

parts.note: to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a university riding in a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood, a period coach.

clue.text: Slated building that's hot inside, hot outside

indicators.note: the second hot is wrapped around the building, which sits within it

parts.note: red-hot, so red stands for hot
an oast is a kiln building for drying hops, hot within

explanation.surface: A building criticised for being stuffy inside and scorching on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a Kent kiln for drying hops, hence 'hot inside'. 'Slated' looks like it is about a roof, but it means harshly criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean harshly criticised, as a reviewer pans a bad show.

clue.text: Downhearted dame soldier ditched

indicators.note: the words are thrown into a ditch, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman is low in spirits after her soldier dumped her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditched' looks like the soldier abandoning the dame, but it signals that DAME and SOLDIER are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone demoralised has lost confidence and spirit, so they are dejected.

clue.text: Country we study after end of travels

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind that final letter
end of picks the final letter of the word travels

parts.note: a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: We go back to our books once our journey is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Brew in a strange establishment serving alcohol

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of these three words appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A peculiar pub where they make their own beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a venue that sells wine and other drinks, a kind of licensed premises.

clue.text: Boring military training in front of gym

parts.note: drill is marching and exercise practice for soldiers

indicators.note: front of takes the opening letter of the word gym

explanation.surface: Tedious army exercises held at the front of the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as tedious, but the definition is making holes, as an oil rig does.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring a hole and drilling one are the same action of cutting through with a turning bit.

clue.text: Chemicals set in ground to catch rodent

indicators.note: the jumbled letters close around the rodent, catching it
ground means crushed, so the letters of set in are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a rat is a common rodent

explanation.surface: Fertiliser chemicals are laid in the earth as a rat trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns SET IN into NITES, and 'to catch' puts RAT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are salts of nitric acid, compounds used as fertiliser.

clue.text: Policeman? You'll see me faced with terrible danger

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word danger is mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A warning that a dreadful threat awaits me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' signals the anagram of the danger. The question mark is there because only a French policeman fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police force, a kind of officer.

clue.text: Charge that's indirect about to be quashed

indicators.note: quashed means cancelled, so the word for about is struck out of indirect

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, used to mean about

explanation.surface: An oblique accusation is about to be thrown out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be quashed' reads as a coming court ruling, but 'about' is RE, removed from INDIRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict is to formally accuse someone of a crime.

clue.text: Girl's father, not a person who can change easily?

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: not means the letter a is left out of what comes before

parts.note: pater is old-fashioned Latin for father

explanation.surface: A daughter's dad is not someone who adapts readily.
explanation.walkthrough: ADA + PATER gives ADAPATER; dropping an A leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter is a person who adjusts to new conditions, with the question mark for the device-like sense.

clue.text: Plant author brought to ball

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in tennis or cricket
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer is introduced to a dance at which a flower is worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance but is LOB, a high tossed ball; ELIA, the author's pen name, is added to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden bedding flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: 'Not dead!' Stanley's first character to find him!

definitions.text: 'Not dead!' Stanley's first character to find him!

parts.note: living means alive, not dead

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Stanley's

parts.note: tone is the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: An explorer relieved to find his quarry still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue alludes to the journalist Henry Stanley, who found the missing explorer in Africa in 1871 with the famous greeting 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish missionary explorer was the man Stanley set out to locate and found alive.

clue.text: Last piece from the organ in social event? That's a relief!

indicators.note: in places the organ and last letter inside the social event

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering

indicators.note: last piece from takes the final letter of the word the

parts.note: the liver is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief when the closing music piece is played at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like a church instrument playing the last piece, but it is a body part; 'in' puts it, after the end of 'the', inside the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance is rescue from danger or distress, a release that brings ease.

clue.text: A scoundrel in charge holding me up at university?

indicators.note: holding means the first group keeps the turned word inside it

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A rogue in authority detains me at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns 'me' in this down clue, and 'holding' keeps it in the middle. The question mark shows the definition is loose: academic life happens at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic describes scholarly matters relating to higher education and colleges.

clue.text: What's excited pro — medal that's awarded for best film

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of pro and medal are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: An agitated professional receives the medal for the year's top movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges PRO and MEDAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palme d'Or is the top prize given at the Cannes Film Festival.

clue.text: Soothing things for baby with cold and sore glands possibly

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters of sore glands may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Comforting remedies for an infant who has a chill and swollen glands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soothing things' looks like medicine for the sick baby, but they are lullabies.
explanation.definitionFit: Cradle songs are lullabies sung to lull an infant to sleep.

clue.text: Shackle military division crossing river

indicators.note: the military division goes across the river, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a legion was a Roman army unit

explanation.surface: A legion of soldiers in chains wades over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside LEGION.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a metal fetter locked round a prisoner's ankle.

clue.text: Observe servant making escape

parts.note: to see is to observe
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: Watch a household servant making a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escape' looks like a getaway, but here it is liquid getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow leaking of liquid out through small openings.

clue.text: Time to interrupt gullible citizen

indicators.note: the time letter breaks into the word for gullible

parts.note: naive means trusting and easily fooled

explanation.surface: A credulous local is cut short by the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a person born in a place, so a local inhabitant or national.

clue.text: Someone in the doctor's surgery has lost one document

indicators.note: has lost means the letter for one is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a patient is someone waiting to see the doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A patient at the GP has mislaid a piece of paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: A doctor's surgery is the British name for a GP's clinic. Dropping I from PATIENT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patent is an official paper granting rights to an invention.

clue.text: Injured wise man taken in by father

indicators.note: taken in by puts the wise man inside the word for father

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
a mage is a magician or learned sage

explanation.surface: A wounded sage is sheltered by a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being tricked, but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged means harmed or hurt, as a wound harms someone.

clue.text: Composer in Paris met an artist

indicators.note: in signals the composer lies within the words Paris met an artist

explanation.surface: A composer is said to have met a painter in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Paris' to the start of 'artist'. Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Smetana wrote the cycle Má vlast, so he is an example of a musical creator.

clue.text: Back in canteen, redo menu for today

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Back in the cafeteria, the menu is being revamped to keep it current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run NREDOM inside 'canteen, redo menu', and 'Back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modern belongs to the present day, current rather than old.

clue.text: Preach when some liar is wicked?

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters of some liar are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Is it hypocritical to lecture others when a liar is sinful?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges SOME LIAR; the question mark marks the surface's irony.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise is to lecture people about right and wrong.

clue.text: About to phone, being concerned

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious, on the point of making a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to phone' reads as someone about to call, but 'About' is CA (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: Caring means feeling concern and kindness for others.

clue.text: Most dangerous mountain on far side of Andes

indicators.note: on means the mountain is placed after the final letter
far side of takes the last letter of the word Andes

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: The deadliest peak lies on the far side of the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountain' leads to EVEREST, which really is in the Himalayas, not the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest means harshest or most serious, as of the gravest risks.
